summary_paragraph: A 54-year-old woman with a history of Crohn’s disease, multiple abdominal surgeries, short bowel syndrome, and PTSD was admitted for right upper quadrant abdominal pain lasting several weeks, described as a constant pressure radiating to the back, with intermittent vomiting and baseline diarrhea. She also reported worsening fatigue and depression. CT scan showed no acute intra-abdominal pathology, a small hiatal hernia, and subcutaneous gas likely from injections. Admission labs revealed hyponatremia (Na 127) and elevated creatinine (1.2), consistent with pre-renal azotemia from dehydration, which resolved with IV fluids. Pain improved to baseline, and the patient opted to defer MRE for adhesions until outpatient follow-up. She remained on home medications including Dilaudid for pain, citalopram for depression, and fondaparinux for SVC syndrome. Anxiety was managed with scheduled team rounds and a PRN diazepam prescription for future imaging. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged with GI and primary care.
problems: Diaphragmatic hernia without mention of obstruction or gangrene
